_doc: Stream E (play-test 1, P19). What people on the roads and in the wilds say: about the time of day, the weather, and what has happened lately (kills, the world boss, deaths, events). Stream A picks and fills a line (a bark) when a player comes near a traveller or folk NPC (data/provinces/travellers.json says which pools each role uses). `pools` = line lists by id; `{token}` = filled from `tokens` below. A line may only be used when EVERY token in it is known for this speaker right now — a line with a missing token is skipped, so every pool also holds token-free lines (except the recent.* / worldboss.* pools, which are only chosen when their context exists). `rules` = how a speaker chooses. Original lines; checked against the banned-name list by tests/E. Play-test 2 (Q18): `place.<set piece id>` pools (said by folk and visitors at that set piece) and the set-piece roles (farmer, orchard_keeper, miller, sexton, foreman, innkeeper, stablehand, trainer).

tokens.name: the speaker's display name
tokens.from: the town the traveller's route started at
tokens.dest: the town the traveller is walking to
tokens.town: the nearest town to the speaker
tokens.zone: a zone name (world boss roaming: the zone it marches on)
tokens.weather: the current weather word in this zone (clear, cloud, rain, fog, storm, snow)
tokens.rare: a named rare killed in this zone in the last hour (deeds)
tokens.player: a player's name: the killer / party leader / top contributor / name on a grave
tokens.place: a dungeon or event place name
tokens.count: a number: deaths this hour, visitors this hour, world boss contributors

rules.weightsNote: recent = the recent.* / worldboss.* pool that fits what happened (only when there is such context; its weight goes to role otherwise). weather = weather.<current>. phase = phase.<dawn|day|dusk|night> (schedules.json clock phases; 'late' counts as night). role = the speaker's role pools from travellers.json `chatter` (incl. road.*). archetype = archetype.<zone archetype>. greet is used for the first bark a speaker gives a given player.
rules.recentNote: Of the recent pools whose context exists, take the first in recentPriority 60% of the time, else any of them. recent.deaths needs count >= 3, recent.busy count >= 5, recent.quiet = no visitors in the zone this hour but the listener.
rules.road: road.leaving within 150 m of the route start, road.arriving within 250 m of the destination, road.onroute between, road.danger when a hostile monster is within 60 m of the route ahead.
rules.noRepeat: Never the same line twice in a row per speaker; keep the last 6 lines per speaker and skip them.
rules.bark: A bark when a player comes within 8 m; at most one bark per speaker per 60 s, at most one per player per 20 s across all speakers.
rules.pairs: Two travellers walking together may trade a line + a reply from `reply` (the second speaker, 1.5-3 s later), at most once a minute per group.
rules.tokens: A line with any token this speaker cannot fill is skipped; if a whole pool is skipped, fall back to role, then phase.

greet: Oh good, someone with a sword.
Don't mind me, I'm just passing.
You look like you know where you're going. Lucky you.
Safe roads. Ha. Listen to me.
Hello, stranger. Stay a stranger, it's healthier.
Another one with a sword. The road's getting crowded.
Evening, morning, whichever. I've stopped keeping track.
If you're selling something, I've no money. If you're buying, I've no goods.
phase.dawn: Cold enough to crack teeth this early.
Up before the birds. The birds are smarter.
Best part of the day. Nothing's bitten me yet.
First light. Everything with teeth goes to bed about now. Mostly.
Fog's still in the hollows. Give it an hour.
Dawn. The hour of regret and porridge.
My knees know it's morning before I do.
I like the road at dawn. Quiet. Wet. Quiet.
phase.day: Long day ahead. Long road too.
Sun's up, so the brigands are too.
Good walking weather, if you like walking. I don't.
Bright enough to see what's coming. That's the trouble with it.
Hot work, this. Hot, dull work.
Nothing worse than a road at noon with no shade.
If I keep this pace I'll be there by supper. I won't keep this pace.
phase.dusk: Getting dark. I'd want a roof soon if I were you.
Dusk. The hounds start singing about now.
I hate this hour. Everything looks like something.
Last of the sun. Make it count.
Lamps'll be lit in town. I can almost smell the stew.
Sun's down behind the hills. Walk faster.
The shadows get long and so does the road.
phase.night: You shouldn't be out here in the dark. Neither should I.
Keep your voice down. Things listen at night.
Night road. Nobody sensible walks a night road.
Can't see my own boots. Hope they're still there.
There's eyes in that hedge. There's always eyes in that hedge.
I'd light a torch but then they'd see me.
Stars are out. Lovely. Terrifying, but lovely.
If I don't make the next town, tell them I tried.
weather.clear: Clear skies. You can see trouble a mile off.
Fine weather. The farmers will find a way to complain about it.
Blue sky all the way to the hills.
Lovely day for it. For what, I couldn't tell you.
Dry roads. My boots thank the sky.
Sun on the fields. Even the crows look cheerful.
Clear as a bell. A bell nobody's ringing, thankfully.
weather.cloud: Clouds coming in. Could go either way.
Looks like rain. Looked like rain yesterday too.
Dull sky, dull road, dull company. Present company excepted.
Flat grey sky. Like walking under a lid.
weather.rain: Wet to the bone and two leagues to go.
Rain. Of course. Why wouldn't it.
Good for the turnips, they tell me. I'm not a turnip.
My pack weighs twice what it did this morning.
Rain keeps the bandits indoors. Small mercies.
Every puddle on this road has my name on it.
If it rains any harder the fish will start walking.
weather.fog: Can't see ten paces. Stay close.
Fog. Things come out of it. Mind that.
I heard something in the fog. Then I heard it stop.
Follow the ruts. Don't follow the lights.
Fog's settled in the low ground. Don't go down there.
You could walk past your own mother in this.
Damp, grey and quiet. The quiet's the bad part.
weather.storm: Storm's coming. Get somewhere with walls.
That's thunder. That's thunder getting closer.
Lightning hit a tree back there. Split it like kindling.
Wind nearly took my hat. And the head under it.
Don't stand under anything tall. Or be tall.
Sky's gone black at midday. Nothing good happens under that.
Every dog in the county is howling.
Storm like this, even the monsters stay home.
weather.snow: Snow. My feet have stopped talking to me.
Tracks in the snow. Big ones. Fresh ones.
Can't tell the road from the field under this.
Snowing again. The pass'll be shut by evening.
Everything's white and quiet. Too quiet.
If you find a frozen courier, that's not me. Yet.
My breath's freezing in my beard.
recent.rare_killed: Heard {rare} is dead. {player} did it. Bought a round, too.
{rare}'s gone. Somebody called {player} put it in the ground.
They say {player} killed {rare}. I'll believe it when I see the head.
No more {rare}. I can take the short way home again.
{player} brought down {rare} this very hour. Folk are talking of nothing else.
{rare} won't be bothering anyone. Ask {player}, they were there.
I saw {player} dragging something back. Said it was {rare}. Smelled like it.
Somebody finally dealt with {rare}. My cousin owes me a coin.
{rare} dead, and the road's quieter for it. For about a day.
recent.elite_killed: {player} beat {boss}. Folk are saying it louder every time they tell it.
{boss} is down. {player}, they say. Never heard of them before today.
Heard {boss} finally met someone tougher. {player}, that was.
{boss}'s lot are leaderless now. That makes them angrier, not nicer.
Somebody saw off {boss}. I'd buy them a drink if I had a coin.
They're singing about {player} and {boss} already. Badly.
{boss} is done. The toll's free this week, I hear.
No more {boss}. Now what will the guards complain about?
recent.boss_killed: {player} and {party} others went down into {place} and came back. That's the strange bit.
{boss} is dead, down in {place}. {player}'s lot did it.
Heard {party} went into {place} and finished {boss}. All {party} came out, too.
{place} is quiet tonight. {boss} won't be climbing out of it.
{player} came up out of {place} with {boss}'s gear. Wouldn't let me touch it.
They cleared {place}. {boss} and all. Took {party} of them.
Somebody finally shut {boss} up. Down in {place}, they say.
{player} led {party} into {place}. Came back muddy and rich.
{boss} is gone. The ground near {place} feels lighter.
Did you hear about {place}? {boss}. Gone. {player}'s party.
recent.dungeon_cleared: {place} was cleared today. There's a banner on the door and everything.
{player} cleared {place}. Left the door open, the oaf.
Somebody went through {place} like a broom. {player}, I think.
{place}'s empty, they say. For now. These places fill up again.
{place} cleared out. The rats will move back in by Tuesday.
{player}'s name is chalked on the {place} door. Bragging, I call it.
{place} is done. I might go and have a look. I won't.
They say {place} is safe now. They said that last time.
{player} came out of {place} carrying more than they went in with.
recent.deaths: {count} buried this hour, round here. Watch yourself.
That's {count} gone today in these parts. The gravedigger's whistling.
{count} dead this hour. Whatever's out there is hungry.
Lost {count} round here already. I'm walking in the middle of the road.
The crows are fat. {count} reasons why.
{count} brave fools down this hour. Don't make it {count} and one.
Heard {count} folk didn't come back today.
{count} graves fresh. Bad hour for it.
It's been a hard hour. {count} hard hours, for some.
Somebody's counting the dead. {count}, last I heard.
recent.busy: Busy round here. {count} adventurers through today, easy.
{count} sword-swingers this hour. The wolves are hiding for once.
Never seen the road so full. {count} of you lot at least.
{count} strangers through already. Good for the inn.
Crowded today. Can't swing a cat. Not that I'd swing a cat.
With {count} of you about, I might actually get home.
{count} heroes this hour. Somebody should charge a toll.
All these adventurers. {count}! The boars are terrified.
Busy, busy. {count} folk in armour and not one of them buys turnips.
The inn's full. {count} of your sort, drinking like it's free.
recent.quiet: Quiet today. Nobody about. I don't like it.
Not a soul on the road. Just me and whatever's in the hedge.
Empty roads. Either it's safe or it's very much not.
You're the first face I've seen all day.
So quiet you can hear the grass grow.
Nobody about. Even the brigands took a day off.
Haven't seen another traveller since dawn.
Quiet as a crypt. And I'd know.
Nobody's been through. The tracks are all old.
recent.zone_event: {event}! Right now! Everybody with a blade is heading that way.
Haven't you heard? {event}. Go on, they need hands.
{event} is happening, and I'm walking the other way.
There's a {event} on. You can hear it from here.
{event}. If you're any good with that sword, now's the time.
Bells ringing for {event}. Run toward it, not like me.
If you want glory, {event}'s where it is. If you want supper, come with me.
{event} going on. I saw the smoke.
recent.zone_event_won: Heard {event} went our way. Drinks are cheap tonight.
{event} is done with. Folk are cheering in town.
We beat {event}. Well, somebody did. I was hiding.
{event} finished. Nobody I know died. Good day.
That {event} business is settled. For now.
Somebody saw off {event}. I'd shake their hand.
{event}'s won. The town's acting like it was their idea.
After {event}, the road feels safer. Feels.
Over and done, {event}. Now back to normal misery.
recent.grave: There's a fresh grave back there. {player}, it says. Poor soul.
Someone's dug a marker for {player}. Not deep, mind.
{player} fell near here. Mind where you step.
Saw a grave with {player} on it. Hope they're up and about again.
{player}'s grave. Short life or short fight, couldn't say.
Fresh earth and a name. {player}. Somebody should leave flowers.
That grave's for {player}. They'll be back, your sort always are.
Passed {player}'s grave. Left a pebble. Seemed right.
Did you know {player}? There's a grave with their name on it.
{player} rests back there. Or sulks. Hard to tell with your lot.
worldboss.soon: {worldboss} wakes in {minutes} minutes. Folk are packing.
They say {worldboss} rises in {minutes}. I'll be indoors.
Waystones to the Scar are free, they say. {worldboss} in {minutes} minutes.
You feel that? {worldboss}. {minutes} minutes, maybe less.
{worldboss} is stirring. {minutes} minutes and it's walking.
Every fool with a sword is off to fight {worldboss} in {minutes} minutes. Go on, then.
{minutes} minutes. Then {worldboss}. Then a lot of graves.
worldboss.up: It's up. The big one. Everybody's running one way and I'm running the other.
The siege-husk is walking. Can you hear it?
That's the world boss, that shaking. Go and help, or go and hide.
It's risen. The whole Scar's on fire with it.
Every waystone's busy. It's up, the big ugly thing.
Something huge is awake out east. Smell that?
They need every blade. I have a spoon. I'm not going.
The big one's up. The birds have all gone quiet.
It's walking. Somebody should stop it. Somebody else.
You'll want to be at the Scar right now, if you're the brave sort.
worldboss.down: {player} landed the killing blow, they say, and {count} others stood with them.
The big one's down! {count} of them took it, {player} at the front.
{count} fighters and {player} brought it down. Drinks on the town.
Heard {player} was first in and last out. {count} with them.
It's dead. {count} heroes and one {player} saw to it.
{player}'s the name on everyone's lips. And {count} others nobody can name.
Down it went. {count} of them. Took most of the afternoon.
The Scar's quiet. {player}'s lot, all {count} of them.
It fell. {count} people say they hit it. {player} actually did.
worldboss.roaming: {worldboss} broke out of the Scar! It's heading for {zone}.
They say {worldboss} is marching on {zone}. Poor {zone}.
Keep clear of {zone}. {worldboss} is on its way.
{worldboss} in {zone}. Haven't seen that in years.
{worldboss} out of its hole and off to {zone}, the brute.
Heard {worldboss} smashed a fence on its way to {zone}.
The big husk is roaming. {zone}'s turn tonight.
road.leaving: {dest} by nightfall, if the road's kind.
Heading for {dest}. Wish me boring luck.
Bound for {dest}. Don't follow me, I'm slow.
I hear {dest} has a decent inn. I'll judge for myself.
road.onroute: {from} to {dest}. Every week. Every blessed week.
Is this the road to {dest}? I came from {from}, so it had better be.
Coming from {from}. They send their regards. They don't, but it's polite.
{from} was dull. Let's hope {dest} is duller.
Walked from {from} with a stone in my boot the whole way to {dest}.
Nothing in {from} worth staying for. Off to {dest}.
road.arriving: Nearly at {dest}. I can smell the bakery.
{dest} at last. My feet are filing a complaint.
Almost in {dest}. First stop, a bench.
{dest}'s walls! Never been so glad to see walls.
Here's {dest}. Not much, but it's got a roof.
Made it to {dest} with all my fingers. Good trip.
road.danger: Something on the road ahead. Teeth, mostly.
Don't go that way. Not alone.
Hounds by the ford. Lots of them.
Brigands up ahead, sitting on the verge like they own it.
Saw shapes in the ditch. Walked faster.
There's a pack sniffing round the bend. Mind it.
Road's not safe past the next hill.
Something big crossed the road ahead. I let it.
reply: I'm not arguing about this again.
That's not how I heard it.
Couldn't agree more. Couldn't agree less, either.
role.merchant: Fine goods, fair prices, unfair roads.
Buy low, sell high, don't get stabbed. Three rules.
Every toll on this road takes a bite. Soon there'll be nothing left to bite.
I'd sell you something but it's all spoken for. And overpriced.
Wool to the river, salt to the hills, debts everywhere.
My ledger and I are not on speaking terms.
If anyone asks, I'm carrying turnips. Only turnips.
Profit's a lovely word. I hear it's lovely.
role.caravan_guard: Eyes front. I'm paid to be suspicious.
Keep your hands where I can see them, friend.
If it comes to it, I run toward the trouble. Slowly.
The pay's bad but the boredom's excellent.
Last brigand who tried us is still picking splinters out.
Don't touch the cart. The cart has feelings.
Nothing's happened all week. I'm starting to take it personally.
role.porter: Carried this pack from one end of the county to the other.
They pay me by the mile, not by the stone. Unfair.
Don't ask what's in the box. I don't know. I don't want to.
One more hill and I'll lie down in it.
Lift with the knees, they say. My knees say otherwise.
role.guard_patrol: Road's clear as far as the bridge.
Report anything with teeth to the watch house.
Keep moving, citizen. Nothing to see. Yet.
We walk it so you don't have to worry. Worry anyway.
Third patrol today. My feet hate this road.
Saw hounds at the tree line. We'll swing back for them.
If you see Hobb's lot, don't be a hero. Fetch us.
On patrol. Which means walking, mostly.
role.pilgrim: Every stone on the road is a prayer. My feet are very devout.
The saint walked this road barefoot. I'm beginning to think the saint was mad.
Walk with us a while? We sing. Badly.
The shrine's three days on. Or a lifetime. Depends who you ask.
I gave up shoes for the pilgrimage. I regret it in every toe.
Blessings on you, stranger. That's free. The candles aren't.
We pray at every crossroads. It's slow going.
The bells at the Rise. You'll hear them before you see them.
role.hunter: Boar tracks by the stream. Big ones.
Hounds have gone bold this year. Too bold.
Wind's wrong for stalking. Might as well walk.
Three days, two rabbits and a cold. Good hunting.
Never chase a boar into a thicket. I have the scars to prove it.
There's something in the wood that isn't deer. Keep out of it.
role.courier: Urgent. Everything's urgent. Nothing's ever urgent.
If this reaches them in time, someone gets married. Or sued.
Out of my way, friend, the reeve wants this yesterday.
Two horses lamed this month. The road eats horses.
Sealed letters. Don't ask. I can't read anyway.
Faster than the post and twice as rude.
Back by sundown, or they dock my pay.
role.drover: Mind the cattle, they mind nothing.
Taking them to market. They don't know. Don't tell them.
This one's called Bessie. That one's called Bessie too. I'm not imaginative.
Lost two to the hounds last week. Keep 'em close now.
Dust, flies and cows. My whole life.
If they bolt, they bolt into the river. Every time.
Slow going. Cattle don't hurry for anybody.
role.minstrel: Want a song? It's about you. It's not flattering.
We've a new verse about the brigands. They didn't like it either.
Three towns, three suppers, no applause.
Tune's in my head and my lute's out of tune.
Heard any good deaths lately? Need new material.
We play weddings, funerals and anything in between.
Every tavern wants the same song. I hate that song.
Our drummer left. We're still finding the rhythm.
role.tinker: Pots mended, knives sharpened, gossip sold.
Bring me anything broken. I'll make it differently broken.
The mule bites. I don't. Usually.
Got a pan with a hole? I've got a hole with a pan.
Old iron, old rope, old news. All cheap.
I've mended half the kettles in this county. The other half are mine.
Need a lock fixed? Need one opened? Different prices.
Every road's my road, every hedge my bed.
role.refugee: We're not going back. There's nothing to go back to.
They burned the barns. Then the houses. Then we stopped watching.
Is there work in town? Any work?
Keep the little one away from the ditch, please.
We had a farm. Now we have a cart.
If you see the folk who did it, you'll know them by the smell of smoke.
Somebody said the town takes people in. Somebody says a lot.
We walk at night when we must. We must, mostly.
role.woodcarter: Logs for the town. Town burns them. I fetch more. Circle of life.
This ox has been on this road longer than me.
Watch the load, it shifts on the hills.
Every winter the town wants twice the wood.
Oak for the smith, ash for the fletcher, pine for whoever complains least.
role.tax_collector: Don't look at me like that. I don't make the rates.
Everybody's poor when they see me coming.
The reeve wants his share, and his share's grown.
I have guards because people love me so much.
A tenth of everything. A tenth of nothing is still nothing, I suppose.
Smile. Taxes pay for the road you're walking on. Some of it.
role.gravedigger: Busy season. It's always busy season.
Six feet, always six. Folk don't come in other sizes.
Your lot keep me in boots, you adventurers.
Quiet trade, mine. My customers don't complain.
Got a shovel and a cart and a lot of patience.
Most of them come back, your sort. Wastes my good digging.
role.woodcutter: Good straight oak. Shame to cut it. Shame not to.
Axe needs sharpening. So does my temper.
The forest takes back everything I cut, given a year.
Something chewed my sawhorse last night. Something big.
Ten trees by dusk or no supper.
Never cut the old ones. They hold grudges.
role.shepherd: Lost three to the hounds. Don't you be the fourth.
Every sheep has a name. Every name is Dolly.
Seen a stray ewe? Big, stupid, black face?
Up the hill, down the hill, up the hill.
My dog does the work. I do the worrying.
Wolves at night, flies by day, wool at shearing. That's the life.
They follow me because they don't know better. Like most followers.
Don't wave your arms, you'll start a stampede. A slow one.
role.herbalist: Feverfew, yarrow, and something I'm not naming.
Don't eat the red ones. Or the white ones. Ask before you eat anything.
This patch cures headaches. That patch causes them.
The best herbs grow where nobody walks. Like here.
Bryn in town pays well for moss. Odd woman.
Mind your feet, you're standing on supper.
Sorrel by the stream, nettle by the wall, mandrake nowhere you'd want.
Three hours for a basket. Worth every sting.
role.prospector: Copper. Or rust. Hard to tell till you bite it.
There's a seam in this hill. I can feel it in my teeth.
Dug a hole. Found a smaller hole.
One more shaft and I'm rich. That's what I said last shaft.
Don't stand there, the bank's loose.
The old miners left the best bits. They always do.
Shiny! No. Mica. It's always mica.
Rock's got secrets. I've got a pick.
role.charcoal_burner: Keep the mound smouldering, not burning. That's the whole trick.
I smell of smoke. Everybody says so. Nobody visits.
Three days to burn a stack. Three days of not sleeping.
The smith buys every sack I make.
Black hands, black lungs, black humour.
role.hermit: Go away. Oh, you're already going. Good.
I came out here for the quiet. You're not quiet.
The trees talk, if you're patient. They're mostly rude.
Want wisdom? Don't go in that cave. There. Free.
I used to live in town. Then I met the people.
Sit if you like. Don't speak.
Seen things out here. Things that don't happen in town.
The stars are better company. They stay where they're put.
role.fisher: There's a big one in there. There's always a big one in there.
Lost my best net to something with more teeth than a fish ought.
Good water this. Too good. Something else fishes it too.
A bucket of eels by noon, or I go home in shame.
My nephew fell in last week. We found him. Mostly the hat.
Patience is a fisher's only tool. Patience and worms.
role.poacher: Those are the reeve's rabbits? Didn't have his name on them.
Snares, not traps. There's a difference. Legally.
Keep walking, friend, and I'll keep not seeing you too.
The lord's deer are my deer when the lord's asleep.
I'm a hunter. With fewer permissions.
role.surveyor: Two hundred paces to the stone. No, two hundred and three.
The old maps put a river here. Rivers move, apparently.
Somebody's moved the boundary stone again. Every year.
The reeve wants a new road. Wants. Hah.
Measuring the county, one argument at a time.
role.scarecrow_maker: This one's called Gerald. Gerald frightens crows and children.
Straw, sackcloth, and a turnip head. Art.
The crows have learned to sit on them. Clever birds.
I make them scarier every year. The crows get braver every year.
Need a scarecrow? I do custom faces. Even yours.
One of mine walked off last spring. I don't talk about it.
role.beekeeper: Calm voices. They don't like shouting.
Honey's good this year. Stings are better.
The hives hum louder before a storm. They're humming now.
Best mead in the county starts right here.
I've been stung so often I'm half bee.
archetype.heartland: Turnips again this year. Turnips forever.
Good soil round here. Too good. Everybody wants it.
The mill wheel's been squeaking for a month.
Harvest coming in. Hounds coming in after it.
Farms, fields, fences. Nothing ever happens. Except when it does.
Somebody's sheep are in somebody else's barley again.
archetype.marsh: Stay on the boards. The bog keeps what it takes.
Lights over the water at night. Don't follow them.
The fen smells like old soup and older secrets.
Everything's damp. My bones are damp. My thoughts are damp.
Croakers singing. Means rain, or means they're hungry.
I've lost two boots to the mud this year.
archetype.crown_ring: The city's grand, if you like being robbed politely.
Banners on every tower. Taxes on every banner.
The crown pays for the roads. The roads pay for the crown.
Busy streets, busy guards, busy pickpockets.
In the city, everyone knows your business before you do.
Market day. Bring coin, hide coin.
archetype.frontier: Edge of the map, this. Past here it's anybody's.
Forts keep falling down. Nobody keeps building them up.
Out here, the law's whoever has the biggest stick.
Cinder imps in the scrub. Don't ask me where they come from.
Hard country. Hard people. Hard bread.
The fort sends patrols when it feels like it.
archetype.wilds: The wood's older than the road. It knows it, too.
Off the path, nobody finds you. Nobody.
Antlers in the thicket. Big antlers. Too big.
Every tree looks like the last tree.
The wilds don't care who you are. Good for them.
archetype.ruinfield: Old stones everywhere. Old dead under them.
Somebody built a kingdom here. Somebody else knocked it down.
Don't dig. Every hole's a grave round here.
The ruins hum at night. I don't go near them.
Good stone for walls, if you don't mind ghosts.
Barrow hounds sleep in the old cellars.
archetype.lakeland: Lake's calm today. Don't trust it.
Fish for breakfast, fish for supper, fish in my dreams.
Something big surfaced out there last week.
The water's so clear you can see the bottom. And what's on it.
Boats go out, mostly come back.
Mist on the lake at dawn. Prettiest thing you'll fear.
archetype.pass: The pass shuts with the first snow. Get through or wait till spring.
Mind the scree. It moves when you don't.
Griffins up on the crags. They like horses. To eat.
Thin air up here. Thin tempers too.
Avalanche last month. They're still digging out the toll house.
archetype.blight: The ground's sick. Don't let it touch you.
Nothing grows right here any more.
The warband burns what it can't carry.
Smells like burnt hair and bad decisions.
archetype.holy_ground: Bells at the Rise every hour. You stop hearing them. Then you can't sleep without them.
Holy ground, they say. The dead don't seem to know it.
Pilgrims everywhere. Pickpockets dressed as pilgrims, too.
Don't spit near the shrine. They fine you.
The saint's bones are in the abbey. Most of them.
Candles cost double here. Holiness isn't cheap.
archetype.mine_country: Hear that rumble? Another shaft gone.
Dust in the bread, dust in the beer.
The old workings go deeper than anybody's maps.
Miners' bell means somebody's trapped. It rings a lot.
Something lives in the deep shafts. The rats left.
archetype.coast: Salt in everything. Even the honey.
Wreckers on the headland. False lights.
The tide takes what it likes.
Gulls'll have your lunch before you've unwrapped it.
Fog off the sea every evening, regular as rent.
Smugglers' coves all along here. Not that I'd know.
place.sp_drill_field: Mind the dummies. They hit back if you lean on them.
Dawn drill, every day. The Sergeant's idea of mercy is a short lunch.
Somebody put a helmet on the third dummy. Now he looks like he outranks us.
Sand in the boots means you've been working. Sand in the teeth means you've been learning.
Every arrow in that fence is somebody's first.
place.sp_brannock_fields: Good soil here. Too good. Things grow that nobody planted.
The scarecrow faces a different way every morning. Nobody moves him. Nobody admits it.
Boars in the turnips again. They know the hedge better than we do.
Apples first, cider second, regret third. Brannock way.
Watch the bees. They're in a mood about the weather.
place.sp_turnwater_mill: The wheel never stops. Not for floods, not for funerals.
Flour in your hair by noon, rats in your dreams by night.
Somebody mends the gearing at night. Hob says he doesn't. Hob sleeps very well.
Hear the stones? That's the sound of bread being argued into existence.
place.sp_saint_hulda_yard: Keep to the path. The grass between graves is for the residents.
The bell rings itself on still nights. Not loud. Just enough.
New grave by the wall. Nobody's died that I know of.
Saint Hulda kept the dead tidy. We try to keep up the standard.
The hounds dig for bones. They're not the only ones.
place.sp_greyfletch_camp: If it walks, we've tallied it. If it walks funny, we've tallied it twice.
Old Gristle took Bess the sheepdog. Uncle Oswy's been sharpening ever since.
Smoke keeps the flies off the meat and the meat off the flies.
Never hunt alone. The tally board has a column for that.
Bring a hide, get a drink. Bring Gristle's hide, get the barrel.
place.sp_gristles_hollow: Smells like wet dog and old murder.
Every bone here was somebody's supper. Don't be the next course.
That den is warm. Something big just left it. Or didn't.
Quiet. The hounds are listening for him to wake.
place.sp_nine_maidens: Count them. Then count again. Never the same number twice, they say.
The wind goes round the ring the wrong way.
Don't step in the mushroom ring. Step round it. You know this.
Nine girls danced on a holy day and the stones caught them. That's the polite version.
The altar holds rain that never dries.
place.sp_kind_mother_shrine: Leave a coin. She doesn't need it, but you'll feel better.
Her hands are warm. Always. Even in frost.
Every pebble in those cairns is a wish. Some of them are rude.
Pilgrims sit here and say nothing for an hour. It's the best hour they get.
place.sp_coldharrow_ruins: The fire was thirty years ago. The stones still smell of it.
Don't stand in the circle in the hall. Your shadow comes back late.
Brigands sleep here because nobody else will.
The Coldharrow girl survived the fire. Some say she lit it.
Old money under the old hearth, if you believe drunks.
place.sp_ashby_lumber_camp: Timber! No. Wait. Not yet. Never mind.
Every tree we drop, the forest sends something to argue about it.
Mind the stumps after dark. They trip you on purpose.
Sawdust in the stew again. Adds body, says the foreman.
The flitters come out at the last hour of light. So we stop at the second-last.
place.sp_tench_pool: Forty years fishing this pool and the croakers turn up like they paid for the place.
Deep water, flat calm. Something down there is thinking.
Sit on the jetty a while. The pool makes people quiet.
Big tench in here. Bigger than you'd credit. Hungrier too.
place.sp_pail_and_plough: Halfway to Orrinsford, halfway home. Have a drink either way.
Ale's brown, stew's brown, the dog is brown. Consistent house.
Read the notice post. There's a bounty on that big hound.
Marra hears everything on this road. Buy a bowl and she might share.
Dice in the corner, songs by the hearth, fights by the door.
role.farmer: Rain for the wheat, sun for the hay, and the two of them never agree.
Every boar in the county knows where my turnips are.
Up before the sun. The sun is a lazy layabout.
The soil's good this year. Suspiciously good.
You want work? There's always work. There's never pay, but there's work.
I talk to the scarecrow. He's the only one who listens.
Mud to the knees and glad of it.
role.orchard_keeper: Apples don't fall far from the tree. Unless the boars get them.
The bees have opinions about everyone. Mostly bad ones.
Good cider takes a year. Bad cider takes a week and a strong stomach.
Never climb a pear tree in a skirt. Lesson learned.
Windfalls for the pigs, the best for the press, the worms for the birds.
An orchard is just a forest that's been taught manners.
role.miller: The wheel keeps turning. So do I. Slower, these days.
Flour gets everywhere. I've been white since I was twelve.
Rats eat the grain, cats eat the rats, the cats eat better than me.
Never trust a miller with clean hands.
Grind fine for bread, coarse for porridge, and never on a feast day.
Water's high this week. Good for the wheel, bad for the cellar.
role.sexton: Somebody has to keep them tucked in.
I ring the bell for the dead. Sometimes they ring it back.
Grass on the graves, weeds on the path, and always one more hole to dig.
Quiet neighbours, mostly. I've lived beside worse.
Mind where you step. Everybody here was somebody.
I know every name in this yard. Some of them know mine.
A good grave is square. A bad one is a story.
role.foreman: Wood doesn't cut itself. I've asked.
Keep your axe sharp and your feet sharper.
Every tree has a way it wants to fall. Learn it or wear it.
Dawn to dusk. Not a minute past. Not after what happened.
I pay by the log. I dock by the finger.
Somebody's been nicking the good wedges again.
role.innkeeper: Rooms are clean. The beds are honest. The fleas are local.
Everyone passes through a crossroads eventually. Most of them owe me.
I hear every rumour on this road. Half of them I started.
Wipe your boots. We've had enough mud from heroes.
Last orders are when I say. I haven't said yet.
Drink up, it's a long way to anywhere.
role.stablehand: Horses are honest. They kick you to your face.
That bay mare bites. That grey one bites harder. Pick a horse.
Leave your mount with me and you'll get it back. Mostly fed.
Duchess the ox is not a horse. Tell her that, I dare you.
Smells like money in here, if money smelled of horse.
role.trainer: Again. And this time like you mean it.
Talent is nice. Practice is better. Bruises are the receipt.
I've trained better than you. I've also trained worse. Mostly worse.
Come back when you've bled a bit. Then we'll talk.
Learn the first lesson well and the rest will find you.
Everyone wants the big tricks. Nobody wants to learn to stand.
Watch your feet. Your feet lose more fights than your hands.
